source.note: This sidecar does not reproduce the source rules text. It records neutral prototype semantics needed to test DODGE gaps.

migration_intent.purpose: Preserve suspected neutral contracts for RPG-shaped semantics that DIRPS may need while targeting DODGE 0.2.1.
migration_intent.rule: At G0 these are hypotheses, not DODGE gaps proven by execution. DIRPS must first pass the selected DODGE version and exercise a concept through shared validation/resolution/runtime before promotion.
migration_intent.target: future DODGE proposal only after candidate evidence exists
promotion_gate: implemented through shared resolver/runtime rather than target-specific code
covered by positive, negative, and perturbation/deterministic tests as applicable
demonstrated to be reusable beyond GURPS-specific terminology
migration_intent.g5_note: G5 exercises only the minimum concepts required by the bounded attempt-skill -> success-roll path. Exercise does not imply DODGE candidacy. The binary <= classifier is explicitly bounded to effective targets 4..16; targets outside that domain fail visibly rather than approximating GURPS edge semantics. Session history, derived values/modifiers, critical-result consequences, and broader RPG semantics remain suspected/unimplemented.
migration_intent.phase_a_note: Phase A executes source-owned contextual modifiers, derives effective target as base skill plus the declared modifier total, classifies GURPS Lite critical success/failure boundaries, and supports deterministic generated 3d6 evidence. The accepted G5 g5_execution_bindings.attempt-skill contract remains unchanged and continues to emit dirps-execution-result.v1. The expanded Phase A contract lives separately under phase_a_execution_bindings.attempt-skill and emits dirps-execution-result.v2, so legacy records remain reproducible and cannot be confused with v2. derived_values and expressions remain suspected because Phase A uses a bounded DIRPS-private execution binding rather than either proposed generic proto shape.
migration_intent.phase_b_note: Phase B composes the accepted Phase A contextual skill result with standard DODGE 0.2.1 scenario runtime-state bindings and structured set effects. The sidecar only bridges the skill outcome branch to ordered DODGE effect refs and one encounter-result evidence record. No new proto concept is promoted; replay_session_history remains suspected because this is still one encounter record, not an append-only session.
migration_intent.phase_c_note: Phase C executes one GURPS Lite reaction roll for a request for information. It uses a declarative lookup table plus deterministic 3d6 evidence and canonical scenario-owned approach/consequence facts. lookup_tables becomes exercised/not-yet-candidate. reaction_timing remains suspected because an NPC reaction roll is not an interrupt/reaction window.
migration_intent.phase_d_note: Phase D reuses the accepted success-roll/dice/procedure-context machinery for a canonical DX-based environmental check and standard DODGE runtime state/effects for consequences. No new proto concept is promoted.
migration_intent.phase_e_note: Phase E executes one bounded attack -> active defense -> damage -> injury sequence. reaction_timing, derived_values, expressions, and damage_injury are exercised from target-neutral sidecar contracts. lookup_tables remains exercised via a bounded ST10 swing-damage lookup. Unsupported combat options fail visibly.
migration_intent.phase_f_note: Phase F resolves the next-turn HT consciousness obligation and physical-stun recovery over the exact Phase E combat runtime state. GURPS Lite owns the HT checks and state consequences; Scenario 01 owns the bounded actor/action/timing/order plus a prototype 0 Strong/Weak Will modifier assumption; DODGE set effects own normalized state mutation; the sidecar only orchestrates the two checks. Long-term recovery from unconsciousness and healing remain unsupported.

dice_resolution.dodge_gap: DODGE 0.2.1 has randomizer objects but no first-class executable roll/resolution primitive that records rolled terms and a deterministic outcome.
dice_resolution.g5_evidence: G5 executes the proposed 3d6 dice-pool/lte success-roll contract from the resolved sidecar using supplied deterministic die terms.
dice_resolution.phase_a_evidence: Phase A adds deterministic generated evidence using the runtime-owned sha256-rejection-v1 algorithm while preserving seed, algorithm id, individual die terms, and total. Supplied explicit die terms remain supported.
dice_resolution.phase_c_evidence: Phase C reuses deterministic supplied/seeded 3d6 evidence for a reaction roll whose higher modified total feeds a lookup table rather than a success-roll comparator.

derived_values.dodge_gap: DODGE 0.2.1 value definitions store typed state but do not define dependency formulas for derived values.
derived_values.phase_a_evidence: Reassessed but not promoted: Phase A computes one effective target inside the bounded attempt-skill execution binding. It does not implement the proposed generic derived-value contract, dependency graph, or recomputation model.
derived_values.phase_e_evidence: Phase E derives the bandit's Dodge target from DX/HT/encumbrance and derives cutting injury from penetrating damage through resolver-preserved expression references.

expressions.dodge_gap: DODGE 0.2.1 conditions/effects provide bounded operators but not a reusable arithmetic expression graph for rules math.
expressions.phase_e_evidence: Phase E executes pure add/subtract/divide/floor expression trees for Dodge target and cutting injury rather than embedding those calculations in the target.

lookup_tables.dodge_gap: DODGE 0.2.1 has no first-class table lookup semantic for rules that map one value/range to another result.
lookup_tables.phase_c_evidence: Phase C executes the GURPS Lite Reaction Table as a target-neutral ordered range lookup from modified reaction total to reaction category. The representation is exercised only in DIRPS and is not yet proposed upstream.
lookup_tables.phase_e_evidence: Phase E uses a bounded authoritative ST-to-swing-damage lookup for the supported ST10 broadsword path.

procedure_context.dodge_gap: DODGE 0.2.1 ordered procedures lack named local variables/outputs that later steps can reference.
dirps_evidence: base target -> modifiers -> effective target -> roll -> margin -> consequence
procedure_context.g5_evidence: G5 requires named actor/skill/random-evidence inputs and emits named target/result outputs for success-roll; this remains a DIRPS-private runtime shape.
procedure_context.phase_a_evidence: Phase A adds context_ref plus resolved modifier inputs and exposes base target, modifier total, effective target, critical classification, and random-evidence provenance.
procedure_context.phase_b_evidence: Phase B carries encounter_ref/action_id/runtime state plus the nested Phase A skill result through one investigation procedure and emits explicit before/after state evidence.
procedure_context.phase_c_evidence: Phase C carries encounter/action identity, resolved reaction modifiers, random evidence, modified total, lookup-table classification, and scenario consequence state through one social procedure.
procedure_context.phase_d_evidence: Phase D carries an attribute-target context (DX), source-owned environmental modifier, runtime state, and ordered success/failure effects through one bounded procedure.
procedure_context.phase_f_evidence: Phase F executes one ordered next-turn recovery procedure: consciousness first when HP <= 0 and the obligation flag is set, then physical-stun recovery only if the actor remains conscious.

reaction_timing.dodge_gap: DODGE 0.2.1 phases and ordered procedures do not explicitly model interrupt/reaction windows or constrained defensive responses.
dirps_evidence: active defenses after a successful attack
reaction_timing.phase_c_evidence: Reassessed but not promoted: GURPS reaction rolls classify NPC attitude; they do not exercise interrupt/reaction-window timing.
reaction_timing.phase_e_evidence: Phase E opens one defense window only after a successful noncritical attack, restricts the responder to the attacked bandit, allows exactly one declared Dodge defense, and closes the window before damage.

visibility_and_secret_state.dodge_gap: DODGE 0.2.1 has no generic visibility contract for GM-only state, hidden checks, or player-visible versus concealed information.

actor_character_model.dodge_gap: DODGE actors can be objects with state, but RPG character structure is currently ad hoc instance state/extensions.
actor_character_model.g5_evidence: G5 runtime selects the resolved actor and reads its resolved character skill bindings; no generic DODGE character model is claimed.

skill_model.dodge_gap: DODGE 0.2.1 has no reusable semantic model for learned skills, defaults, governing attributes, or resolved levels.
skill_model.g5_evidence: G5 executes one explicitly resolved skill level as the target; governing attributes, defaults, and a full generic skill model remain unimplemented.

resolution_trace.dodge_gap: DODGE 0.2.1 describes rules but not a standard evidence record showing which rules, modifiers, random terms, and state changes produced a result.
resolution_trace.g5_evidence: G5 emits a structured execution record linking action, procedure, target, die evidence, result/margin, and source authority.
resolution_trace.phase_a_evidence: Phase A adds modifier-by-modifier provenance, effective-target derivation trace, critical classification source trace, and generated-random seed/algorithm evidence.
resolution_trace.phase_b_evidence: Phase B records the selected encounter action, nested v2 skill resolution, ordered DODGE consequence effect refs, exact state delta, and before/after neutral runtime state.
resolution_trace.phase_c_evidence: Phase C preserves reaction modifier provenance, 3d6 terms, raw/modified totals, reaction-table source/row, consequence effects, and before/after neutral state.
resolution_trace.phase_d_evidence: Phase D records attribute target provenance, modifiers, dice evidence, success classification, ordered DODGE effects, and exact before/after environmental state.
resolution_trace.phase_f_evidence: Phase F preserves each executed HT roll, target/modifier provenance, skipped-check reason, normalized DODGE effect refs, and exact before/after combat state.

replay_session_history.dodge_gap: DODGE 0.2.1 has no first-class immutable session/replay sequence comparable to the Wretched replay contract.
replay_session_history.phase_b_evidence: Reassessed but not promoted: Phase B deterministically re-evaluates one stateful encounter record. It still does not define an immutable append-only multi-step session history.
replay_session_history.phase_f_evidence: Reassessed but not promoted: deterministic replay covers one recovery-turn record over a Phase E combat snapshot, not an append-only multi-step session.

damage_injury.dodge_gap: DODGE 0.2.1 has typed actor state and effects but no first-class combat damage profile tying weapon/ST damage, DR, damage type, injury multiplier, HP loss, and injury thresholds into one executable result.
dirps_evidence: bounded broadsword cutting injury in Scenario 01
damage_injury.phase_e_evidence: Phase E executes one ST10 broadsword swing/cutting path with DR0, HP subtraction, major-wound stun, and deferred consciousness-check state.

effective_target.rule_locator: p. 2, Success Rolls; Modifiers and Effective Skill

damage.rule_locator: pp. 18-19, Weapon Damage; pp. 26-28, Damage and Injury

stun_recovery.rule_locator: p. 27, Stunning; p. 26, Knockdown and Stunning
